events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
The rider named a specific place — "Can you stop at Clementi Mall?" [F9] — and the driver agreed before the deviation began [F10]; the car did stop, stationary 4 min 0 s at 14:23–14:27 inside the off-route window [F2][F4]. Under RD-3(a), when the rider names the place and the car stops there, the whole segment driven to reach it is not a detour, so the segment's 1.70 extra km (3.80 km driven vs 2.10 km optimal) are exempt in full [F4][RD-3]. The trace's only open element is this RD-3(a) naming question, and F9 answers it: "Clementi Mall" is a named place, not a vague "a 7-Eleven on the way". The recorded stationary point is on the corridor toward that named stop [F2][RD-3].

The driver did not rely on a traffic excuse: bands 4 and 5 with no incidents [F12][F13][F14] fail RD-4(a) and RD-4(b) cannot exempt on its own; RD-5 also fails because no route-change proposal preceded the deviation [F4][RD-4][RD-5]. Those routes are therefore closed, but they are not needed — RD-3(a) alone disposes of F4.

With no unexempted segment, RD-2 yields a refund of 0 for the RydeTAXI distance component; the correct outcome is listed by the trace as no_action [F4][RD-2]. The metered distance of 10.6 km, the $14.88 distance line and the $2.79 excess [F1][F5][F8] all price kilometres driven to the rider's own named stop, so nothing is refundable [RD-2][RD-3].

The $1.04 waiting item is the meter's waiting unit (4.0 min × $0.26/min) for the stop the rider requested, and RD-3(c) preserves metered waiting units on RydeTAXI; both advocates concede this item, so it stands [F2][F6][RD-3]. claims.assertion: This was a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter, so extra kilometres driven are extra fare charged (F8 shows distance $14.88 for 10.6 km at $1.41/km); the trip ran 10.6 km against an 8.6 km optimal route, +2.0 km / +23%.
One off-route segment is recorded: 14:21–14:30, 3.80 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.10 km, adding 1.70 km and straying up to 555 m from the optimal route (F4).

The rider's stop request was for Clementi Mall by name (F9) and the driver accepted it (F10); the recorded stationary period is 14:23–14:27 at a point 3,159 m from pickup and 2,452 m from drop-off (F2), consistent with the named stop rather than an unexplained diversion. Under RD-3(a) a rider-named stop is not itself a detour.

The driver's written statement (F11) offers only the Clementi Mall stop as explanation; it does not explain the 3.80 km off-route segment of which the stop accounts for a small part, so the balance of the off-route kilometres is unexplained and unexempted.

No traffic incident is recorded near the route in the trip window (F14), so no RD-4(a) exemption applies to the off-route segment; the speed bands present (F12, F13) are bands 4 and 5, far from the band 1–2 congestion the policy contemplates.

The rider is claiming only the detour overcharge; since the ride is metered, the refund is the unexempted extra kilometres at the trip's per-km rate: 1.70 km × $1.41/km = $2.397, i.e. $2.40, which the fare table supports as the per-km rate ($14.88 ÷ 10.6 km).

The driver pressed/logged waiting time of 4.0 min billed $1.04 (F6); on RydeTAXI the policy says metered waiting units for the stop remain chargeable (RD-3(c)), so the rider does not contest this item.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes both upheld, including 2 route disputes (F17); with a finding against the driver in this case the account-history condition in RD-6 is met, so an account flag is warranted as an additional action.

weaknesses: The recorded 4 min stop at 14:23–14:27 (F2) sits inside the off-route window (F4), so the driver will argue the whole 1.70 km extra was consumed by the rider's own Clementi Mall request, which the rider did make by name (F9) and the driver accepted (F10) — RD-3(a).

The off-route segment covers 3.80 km while the stop is only 4 minutes; the driver may point out the rider named the destination (F9) and that any additional kilometres beyond that cannot be separately broken out from F1/F4, weakening any claim larger than the segment figure.
The rider's own profiling shows 1 prior dispute with 0 upheld (F16), which the driver can use to attack the rider's credibility on fare complaints.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment (14:21–14:30, +1.70 km) coincides with the rider-requested stop: the rider asked to stop at Clementi Mall at 14:17 and the driver agreed at 14:17, before the segment began, so the deviation to the named place is the rider's own routing request and not an unexcused detour.

The stationary period is 4 min 0 s (14:23–14:27) exactly matching the rider's own stated '3-4 minutes' stop, so the driver's conduct matches the agreed scope; as this is RydeTAXI the stop time is charged on the meter's waiting unit and is not refundable.

Under RD-2 the RydeTAXI refund is confined to the extra distance of the unexcused segment measured against the rider's specified stop, and the rider's requested stop was a named place, so the 1.70 km segment distance is excused and no mileage refund arises; the billed distance component is the standard metered distance charge, not an unannounced extra.
The $1.04 waiting charge is the metered waiting unit (4.0 min × $0.26/min) for the rider-requested 4-minute stop, which RD-3(c) preserves for RydeTAXI.
The driver has no record of route violation being established in this case (no unexcused segment survives RD-3), so RD-6's account referral does not attach here.

weaknesses: The system records show a genuine 1.70 km off-route segment (F4) and total actual distance 10.6 km vs 8.6 km optimal (F1), which the rider will use to argue the stop request did not authorise a 555 m deviation from the optimal route; RD-3(b) could be invoked if the stop's exact location is judged to be the driver's choice rather than the rider's named place.

The traffic record shows only moderate congestion (F12 band 4, F13 band 5) and no incidents (F14), so the driver cannot rely on RD-4 to excuse any part of the deviation, and the unchallenged 2.0 km billed excess (F5, $2.79) is the anchor the rider will press.

The driver's profile shows 2 of 2 disputes upheld in 90 days including 2 route disputes (F17), which the rider can use to seek a flag_account under RD-6 even though the profile cannot decide this case.

points.response: RD-3(a) excuses only the stop the rider named, not the route taken to it: the rider's request was 'stop at Clementi Mall' (F9), yet the recorded segment drove 3.80 km where the optimal route covers 2.10 km and strayed up to 555 m off the optimal route (F4), which is a routing change the rider never asked for. RD-5 requires agreement before the deviation, and F9/F10 show agreement to a stop only, not to a detour of this length.

Conceded: the 4 min 0 s stationary period (F2) matches the rider's stated 3-4 minute stop, and on RydeTAXI metered waiting units for a stop remain chargeable (RD-3(c)); my brief already does not contest the $1.04 waiting item (F6).

RD-3's exemption is per segment and covers only the distance attributable to the named stop; the segment added 1.70 km while the drop-off is unchanged and the rider's request was a parcel stop, so the excess over the agreed scope stays an unexempted segment under RD-2, refundable at the trip's per-km rate of $1.41 ($14.88 ÷ 10.6 km, F8). The driver's own admitted weakness that RD-3(b) may apply to the stop's exact location reinforces this.
Conceded: the $1.04 is the metered waiting unit for the 4-minute stop (F2, F6) and RD-3(c) preserves it for RydeTAXI; the rider does not seek this item back.

An unexempted segment does survive: the 1.70 km extra (F4) is unexplained by the named stop and unexcused by traffic (F14 shows no incidents; F12/F13 are bands 4-5, not the band 1-2 contemplated by RD-4), so RD-2 refund is positive. The driver's 90-day record of 2 upheld route disputes (F17) then satisfies RD-6's account-history condition for a flag_account as an additional action only.

The +2.0 km is metered distance, not an unexplained diversion: the meter simply records what was driven to reach the rider's own named stop at Clementi Mall, and the $14.88 distance line (F8) prices those kilometres at the standard $1.41/km — RD-2 only refunds extra kilometres on segments with no exemption.

The 1.70 km segment (F4) runs 14:21–14:30 and contains the rider's own 14:23–14:27 stop (F2) at a point 3,159 m from pickup, i.e. on the way to the rider-named Clementi Mall; under RD-3(a) a rider-named stop is not a detour, so this segment carries an exemption.
The rider's own brief concedes the named-stop exemption under RD-3(a) (F9, F10, F2); the driver does not need a further explanation for the same segment once the rider-named stop is exempt.

Where the driver does explain (F11: driving to and waiting at Clementi Mall at the rider's request) the system record corroborates him — a 4 min 0 s stationary period inside the off-route window (F2, F4) — and the rider's own message set the 3–4 minute stop (F9), so the segment is accounted for, not unexplained.

The driver does not rely on RD-4: the case is decided by the RD-3 rider-requested stop exemption, so the absence of incidents (F14) and the moderate bands (F12, F13) are irrelevant to why the deviation occurred.

The $2.40 calculation is only correct if the segment is unexempted, but the segment is exempt under RD-3(a)/(c) because it is the route to and the waiting at the rider's named Clementi Mall stop (F9, F10, F2); with no unexempted segment RD-2 yields a refundable amount of 0 and the correct action is no_action.
Accepted: the $1.04 metered waiting unit for the rider-requested 4-minute stop (F2, F6) is chargeable on RydeTAXI under RD-3(c) and the driver does not seek to change it.

RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach); since the deviation is exempt under RD-3 there is no such finding, and the profile counts (F17) cannot create one on their own.

Clarification of the driver's own case: RD-3(c) is invoked only to preserve the metered waiting unit (F6), not to justify the whole segment; the segment itself is exempt because it is the route to the rider-named stop under RD-3(a), and no fare item outside the meter was added (F8).
